content: 1. Sulfisoxazole and Ethinyl Estradiol: Sulfisoxazole reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Ethinyl Estradiol and Tacrolimus: Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Tazemetostat and Ethinyl Estradiol: Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Tecovirimat and Ethinyl Estradiol: Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor the effectiveness of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates when co-administered. 5. Teriflunomide and Ethinyl Estradiol: Teriflunomide increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Tetracycline and Ethinyl Estradiol: Tetracycline reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Ethinyl Estradiol and Theophylline: Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of theophylline by inhibiting hepatic CYP1A2 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 8. Ferrous Fumarate and Thyroid Desiccated: Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of thyroid desiccated by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Tigecycline and Ethinyl Estradiol: Tigecycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Ethinyl Estradiol and Tinidazole: Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Ethinyl Estradiol and Tizanidine: Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of tizanidine by inhibiting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects of tizanidine, such as hypotension or bradycardia. 12. Ethinyl Estradiol and Tolterodine: Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Ethinyl Estradiol and Triazolam: Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of triazolam by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ethinyl estradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to increased serum concentrations of co-administered benzodiazepines. 14. Trientine and Ferrous Fumarate: Trientine and ferrous fumarate mutually decrease each other's levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 15. Trimethoprim and Ethinyl Estradiol: Trimethoprim decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Ethinyl Estradiol and Ursodiol: Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of ursodiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 17. Vadadustat and Ethinyl Estradiol: Vadadustat increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol through an unspecified mechanism. Vadadustat may also increase the exposure of BCRP substrates. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels or effects of vadadustat by binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer vadadustat at least 1 hour before oral iron supplements or iron-containing products. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 18. Ethinyl Estradiol and Valoctocogene Roxaparvovec: Both agents may increase each other's effects through an unspecified mechanism. Medications that may cause hepatotoxicity when combined with valoctocogene roxaparvovec could potentiate the risk of elevated liver enzymes. Monitor closely and consider alternative medications if potential drug interactions are identified. 19. Vonoprazan and Ferrous Fumarate: Vonoprazan decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 20. Acetazolamide and Ethinyl Estradiol: Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown.
